# Guidance patterns in five AP Statistics videos

**Scope.** A purposive spot check of five English auto-generated transcripts: Topic 1.2 Variables, Topic 1.13 Experimental Design, Topic 2.10 Binomial Distribution, Topics 3.6–3.7 P-values and a population proportion test, and Topic 5.4 Residuals. The counts below describe only these five videos. Timestamps are starting points for checking the original videos.

| Guidance type | In sample | What to preserve | Examples |
|---|---:|---|---|

## Recommended resource structure

Store each useful point as one **guidance entry** linked to its video and AP topic. Give each entry: type, one-sentence takeaway, when to use it, steps or conditions if applicable, exam wording if applicable, common error, source timestamp, visual reference, and verification status. A video page can show entries in viewing order. A topic page can combine entries from multiple videos and remove duplicates.

The first pass should collect candidates. A second pass should check the video at each timestamp and verify the statistical claim against the current AP framework. Several transcript lines are simplified or stronger than AP exam language warrants. For example, random assignment tends to balance groups but does not guarantee it; a large p-value does not establish the null hypothesis as true. Preserve the useful teaching move while correcting the final wording.
